newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen weak on liquidity tightening.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen weak on liquidity tightening.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen weak on Tuesday as the government is expected to announce new measures to further tigthen rupiah liquidity, brokers said.
"The expected announcement would further weaken sentiment. Players are worried the move could push interest rates higher," one broker with a foreign brokerage said.

Minister of Economics, Finance and Supervisor of Development, Saleh Afiff, was quoted as saying the tightening would trigger the selling of dollars in favour of the rupiah, allowing the local currency to strengthen.
On Monday, the composite index closed 2.93 percent, or 18.07 points, down at 599.64 points after plunging to an intra-day low of 565.78 points in the morning.
Among stocks to watch were state-controlled firms Telkom, Timah and BNI on market talk that the government would further support the market by buying shares, brokers said.
